## Data Sources{#data-sources}

The Groundfish Assessment Program and the Shellfish Assessment Program conduct the Bering Sea surveys each summer. Haul-level catch data are expanded to CPUE, population abundance, abundance-at-length, abundance-at-age, and biomass estimates. These results are presented in this document, which is produced using R and R Markdown (v`r R.version$major`.`r R.version$minor`). For earlier survey results, see AFSC technical memoranda on the NOAA repository^[https://repository.library.noaa.gov/], the AFSC website^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/resource/publication-database/alaska-fisheries-science-center-technical-memorandums], and the Groundfish Assessment Program website^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/alaska/science-data/groundfish-assessment-program-bottom-trawl-surveys].

Several tools used in this report were developed through the AFSC Groundfish Assessment Program. Distribution maps were generated by the *akgfmaps* package^[https://github.com/afsc-gap-products/akgfmaps] (v`r packageVersion("akgfmaps")`). Temperature patterns and the cold pool figures were created by the *coldpool* package^[https://github.com/afsc-gap-products/coldpool] (v`r packageVersion("coldpool")`). Design-based biomass and abundance indices were calculated using the *gapindex* package^[https://github.com/afsc-gap-products/gapindex] (v`r packageVersion("gapindex")`). Improvements to the production-level data tables and from this data report to the last data report are described in the [Data Changes Appendix](#data-changes).  

Catch, environmental, and location data are available through FOSS^[https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/foss], while biomass and composition estimates are provided through AKFIN^[https://www.psmfc.org/program/alaska-fisheries-information-network-akfin]. NOAA survey data also support DisMAP^[https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/dismap], and additional information is available through ACEPO^[https://shinyfin.psmfc.org/acepo/] and the Human Dimensions Explorer^[https://reports.psmfc.org/akfin].

## Acknowledgments{#acknowledgments}

Recognition and appreciation are extended to the captains and crews of the `r text_list(paste0(vessels$vessel_ital[vessels$vess_shape != "X"], " (", vessels$company[vessels$vess_shape != "X"], ")"))`; Appendix Tables `r ifelse(srvy == "EBS", "C", "E")` \@ref(tab:tab-participants-vessel)). By providing the vessels and maintaining safe operations throughout, they contribute essential expertise that support every phase of the work. Their professionalism, dedication, and commitment to safety make this survey possible. We also extend sincere thanks to the scientists, researchers, contractors, interns, and volunteers whose efforts aboard each vessel ensured the survey was completed safely and successfully (Appendix Tables `r ifelse(srvy == "EBS", "C", "E")` \@ref(tab:tab-participants-sci)). Support from [other AFSC groups](#survey-participants) was vital to planning, execution, and data processing. `r ifelse(report_title == "data", paste0("Finally, appreciation is extended to ", readLines(con = paste0(dir_out_rawdata, "/0-acknowledgments-authors.Rmd"))[1], " for reviewing this document. ", collapse = ""), "")`

We also thank the many Bering Sea communities whose knowledge, experience, and feedback help guide and strengthen this document, highlighting locally important issues and species. This document was prepared in the greater Seattle area, on the traditional lands of the Coast Salish peoples, including the Duwamish. This research was conducted on the traditional homelands of the Inupiat, Yupiit, Siberian Yupiit, Unangax, Alutiiq/Sugpiaq, Eyak, Dena’ina Athabascan, Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian peoples. We honor their stewardship and deep connections to these lands and waters.
